tree.label: tree
tree.answer:
Based on the fetched text, Buffett described Berkshire's **"not-so-secret weapon"** as **Berkshire's ability to immediately respond to market seizures with both huge sums and certainty of performance**.

In the section titled "Our Not-So-Secret Weapon" (page 9), Buffett explains that occasionally markets and/or the economy will cause stocks and bonds of large, fundamentally good businesses to be strikingly mispriced. He notes that markets can unpredictably seize up or even vanish (as they did for four months in 1914 and a few days in 2001). 

Berkshire's weapon is its capacity to act when these market panics occur: *"Berkshire's ability to immediately respond to market seizures with both huge sums and certainty of performance may offer us an occasional large-scale opportunity."* 

This means that when markets freeze up in panic (like during September 2008), Berkshire can deploy massive amounts of capital with certainty to take advantage of the resulting mispricings—opportunities that other market participants, constrained by liquidity or uncertainty, cannot act on.
tree.gt_rationale: The candidate answer accurately identifies the core idea of being able to respond to market seizures with large sums and captures the specific historical examples mentioned in the ground truth.
